failed: WRITE FROM THE DISQUALIFIED VIEWER'S SIDE
Before you write, picture one real person who failed someone badly and thinks there is no way back. Write so that person feels seen in the first two seconds, is never shamed, and leaves lifted up.
depth: Mine John 21:1-17 (and John 18) for the details most people skip (the second fire of coals, the night of nothing, 'Children', 'Come and dine', the third time, 'Feed my sheep', Mark 16:7's 'and Peter'). Build the film on the richest detail you find.
hook: Most viewers decide in 2 seconds. Write the strongest honest hook you can and make every line pull to the next. The payoff must be worth the wait.
plain: Write so a viewer with school English and no Bible knowledge understands every line on first hearing, and a lifelong Bible reader still learns something.
judge: Write the best film you can. Use your own judgment on everything.
